result:
Perfect! The app builds successfully. I've created the complete hero domain layer as specified:

## What I built:

**`src/app/domain/hero.model.ts`** — Hero interface carrying the fields needed by roster and detail screens:
- `id`, `name`, `alias`, `powerClass`, `powerIndex` (0-100), `status` (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), `clearanceTier`, `missionCount`, `successRate`, and optional `bio`

**`src/app/domain/hero.service.ts`** — In-memory signal-based HeroService marked plainly as example data:
- Holds the 12-hero roster from the build spec (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian)
- Provides `all()` and `count()` computed signals
- Exposes `byId(id)` lookup, `update()`, `retire()`, and `add()` methods

**`src/app/domain/hero.schema.ts`** — Zod schema for the hero edit form:
- Fields: name, alias, powerClass, powerIndex, bio, status
- Validation rules bundled on the schema
- Field labels and control kinds live on schema via `.meta()` (single source of truth, no parallel config)
- Exports `HeroModel = z.infer<typeof schema>` for type safety

**`src/app/domain/index.ts`** — Barrel export for cleaner imports

The app builds cleanly with no errors. Ready for the screens to read from this domain.
